source.title: SafeTuneBed: A Toolkit for Benchmarking LLM Safety Alignment in Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Saad Hossain; Samanvay Vajpayee; Sirisha Rambhatla

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning safety-aligned models changes harmful-request outcomes, using its own fine-tuning regimes, task datasets and safety evaluations rather than establishing an exact reproduction of the original recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper's own benchmark experiments measure safety after benign and harmful fine-tuning. The text reports several aggregate results and an Alpaca example. Figure 2 also plots task-specific outcomes, but the individual bar values are not stated in text and cannot be assigned reliably from the supplied figure. The study does not measure token-position KL, compliant-prefix or suffix bypasses, safety-localizing weights, causes of shallowness, or safety-deepening methods.
record.test_reason: The study LoRA-fine-tunes Llama-2-7b-chat on benign data and on data mixed with 5% or 30% BeaverTails harmful examples. It measures AdvBench keyword ASR and a GPT-4o-mini harmfulness score, close to the original setup but with mixed poisoning. The paper is mainly a benchmark toolkit, and most of its text compares defenses (LISA, Vaccine).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that ASR and harmfulness rise with poison ratio for all methods, that LISA degrades most gracefully under poisoning but worse under benign data, and that utility (MMLU, MT-Bench) stays stable. Their main conclusion is that SafeTuneBed enables standardized comparison of defenses.
record.recipe_differences: Uses aligned-model LoRA fine-tuning and harmful-data injection with ASR and harmfulness evaluations, but varies task datasets and poisoning levels and benchmarks multiple defenses. The text does not establish an exact match to the original study's full recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with poisoning level, fine-tuning method and downstream dataset; the text provides some aggregate ranges and an Alpaca-specific comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Under 30% poisoning, LISA keeps Alpaca ASR at 18.6% and harmfulness at 2.01, versus 38.5% and 3.53 for LoRA. Vaccine converges with LoRA. Under benign fine-tuning, LISA shows higher harmfulness (up to 3.04; ASR up to 39%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-training safety defenses such as LISA reduce, but do not prevent, safety loss from harmful fine-tuning, and can cost safety under benign fine-tuning.

record.problems: The supplied text does not give uncertainty estimates for the reported safety values. Several outcomes are reported only as aggregate ranges, without per-task or method-specific assignments; task-level results in Figure 2 are not stated numerically in text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 includes task-specific safety bars for benign, 5% and 30% harm, but the provided figure does not yield reliably assignable numeric values for each model, task and measure; those values are not transcribed as rows.

untested.parts: That a few to a few hundred harmful examples suffice: poisoning here is 5% or 30% of datasets of 1,000 to 50,000 examples. Near-total removal of refusal is not reached. Comparison against the unfine-tuned model is not reported numerically. Only Llama-2-7b-chat is tested.
Benign vs no-fine-tuning comparison: Figure 2 plots it, but the text gives no numbers.
Not studied (SafeLoRA appears only in Figure 2, with no stated values).

missing.what: No-fine-tuning baseline ASR and harmfulness per task, needed to judge V2 and the size of the V1 effect
Per-task LoRA ASR and harmfulness under benign, 5% and 30% poisoning

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a toolkit paper; the safety results are a demonstration with few numbers given in text. The appendix claims results are averaged over three seeds, but no variance is reported. Only one model is used, and keyword-based ASR is coarse. Figure 2 also includes SafeLoRA and 'No fine-tuning' bars that the text never quantifies.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful-data injection at 5% and 30%; it does not establish that a few to a few hundred harmful examples are sufficient, nor report refusal being removed almost entirely.
Includes benign fine-tuning and reports safety outcomes, but does not state a numeric benign-versus-no-fine-tuning comparison in the text.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training safety beyond early response tokens and testing its durability.

rows.note: Reported as an across-task trend on AdvBench; the text does not provide per-task values. The increase is substantial but does not show refusal removed almost entirely.

relationships.reason: ASR rises from 13% to at most about 62% and harmfulness from 1.85 to about 3.5 (r1, r2, r6, r9). The rise is clear but incomplete, even with thousands of harmful examples.
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose from 13% to at most about 62% and harmfulness from 1.85 to about 3.5, a clear but incomplete rise even with thousands of harmful examples.
